$comment: The standards, machine-readable. Hooks and the page-critic agent read this file; humans and models read the prose version in CLAUDE.md. Adding a rule here makes page-critic enforce it with no code change. Keep this list SHORT -- a standard nobody remembers is not a standard.

rules.title: Every path is relative
rules.rule: Use ./ or ../ for every href, src, import and navigation target. Never a root-absolute path.
rules.why: vite.config.js sets base: "./" which is the only reason sub-directory deploys work. A root-absolute path resolves against the host root, so it silently escapes /preview/<topic>/ and /stage/ and lands the user on production.
rules.knownViolation: src/script.js:52-125 -- homepage canvas planet links are /arcade/<game>. Deliberately left; the hook stops the next one.
rules.escape: Add the comment guard:allow-absolute on the same line if you genuinely need it.
rules.$routePrefixes: Top-level site paths. Read by BOTH .claude/hooks/guard.mjs and eslint.config.js -- add a route here and both pick it up with no code change.

rules.title: Runtime dependencies are an allowlist
rules.rule: package.json "dependencies" may contain ONLY the packages named in `allowed` below. devDependencies are fine. Adding a name to `allowed` needs an ADR in the same change.
rules.why: This is a static site on GitHub Pages. Every runtime dep ships to every visitor, and the failure mode is silence -- nobody notices the bundle grew. The list was empty until ADR-025 admitted three.js for the planet background; keeping it a list rather than a boolean means the next one is a decision someone had to write down, not a diff nobody read.
rules.$allowed: Read by .claude/hooks/guard.mjs. Adding a name here is what unblocks the hook -- do it in the same commit as the ADR that justifies it, never on its own.
rules.adr: DECISIONS.md ADR-025 -- three.js, bundled by Vite rather than loaded from a CDN.

rules.title: A page exists when the build emits it
rules.rule: After adding or moving an HTML file, confirm it appears in dist/.
rules.why: vite.config.js builds rollupOptions.input from globSync("**/*.html"). Routing is the filesystem, so a page that is not in dist/ does not exist -- and nothing else will tell you.

rules.title: tailwind.css loads last
rules.rule: Head order is: page CSS -> icon CSS -> tailwind.css. Always last.
rules.why: tailwind.css carries the shared component layer (.pill, .topbar, .badge, .stat, .gameover) and loading last means it wins on equal specificity. Reordering silently restyles eight in-game HUDs.
rules.trap: .topbar { pointer-events: none } in tailwind.css broke the About-me back arrow. Sidestep with a new class -- see src/index.css:104 for the documented precedent. Never edit the shared rule.

rules.title: Decorative canvas is hidden; focus is visible
rules.rule: Every decorative canvas and ornament carries aria-hidden="true". Interactive elements have a focus-visible outline in --color-red.
rules.why: The pages are almost entirely canvas. Without aria-hidden a screen reader walks a wall of nothing, and without focus rings the site is unusable by keyboard.

rules.title: prefers-reduced-motion is the ONLY motion fallback
rules.rule: Gate motion on prefers-reduced-motion. Never gate it on viewport width.
rules.why: Disabling parallax below 760px was an incident fix that treated a symptom -- the real bug was per-letter scatter during scroll. PR #53 root-caused it and removed the width gate. Reintroducing one re-creates the incident.
rules.pattern: html.static-home flattens the journey and calls updateHeadline(1) once; html.js-anim hides un-split words so the name never flashes static.

rules.title: One rAF loop per page, scroll effects are pure functions of p
rules.rule: A page has exactly one requestAnimationFrame loop. Scroll listeners are { passive: true } and only set scrollPos plus a dirty flag. Every scroll effect is a pure function of p = scrollPos / journeyEnd, clamped to [0,1].
rules.why: The clamp is what makes letters settle and hold instead of re-scattering later in the scroll -- it is the whole trick, and removing it was the other half of the PR #53 regression. Multiple loops fight each other and cost frames.

rules.title: The canvas contract
rules.rule: Fixed virtual resolution BASE_W/BASE_H with letterboxed viewScale/viewOffX/viewOffY. dpr = Math.min(devicePixelRatio || 1, 2). ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0) after every resize. Pointer input via screenToWorld(clientX, clientY). dt = Math.min(33, ts - last) * 0.001.
rules.why: Uncapped DPR melts phones. An unclamped dt explodes the simulation on the first dropped frame or backgrounded tab. Virtual resolution is what makes one game readable on a 320px phone and a 1440px desktop.

rules.title: Rule of three
rules.rule: Two copies are fine when the variants genuinely differ. A third occurrence means stop and propose an extraction -- do not extract silently as a side effect of another change.
rules.why: Replaces the old 'pragmatic duplication' stance from AGENTS.md, which canonised triplicated drawPlanet as a virtue. It stopped being one at 14 pages.
knownClusters: back-pill CSS x4 -- src/index.css, src/about-me/about-me.css, src/space-bar/space-bar.css, src/arcade/arcade.css
starfield init x5 -- including one inlined in src/scoreboard/index.html:43-87
rules.resolved: drawPlanet was a x3 cluster (script.js, arcade/arcade.js, arcade/shared/starfield.js) -- resolved by #61's shared PlanetBody class (see the reuse-threejs-universe rule below), not by extraction. One isolated 2D-canvas copy remains in nebula-trail.js, which is a single usage, not a cluster.

rules.title: Design tokens are sole-sourced
rules.rule: Colours, type, spacing, radii and motion come from the @theme block in tailwind.css, mirrored in tokens.ts. Nothing hardcodes a colour.
rules.why: One palette, one place. tokens.ts gives JS a typed handle on the same names so components stop guessing.
rules.exception: The scoreboard sub-palette (--color-scoreboard-*) is a deliberate, documented drift. Leave it.

rules.title: Styling lives in JS from here on
rules.rule: New components carry Tailwind utility classes in their JS/TS templates. Do not add new page-local .css files. The 14 existing ones are frozen -- they keep working, they just stop growing.
rules.why: Utility classes in JS is the shape React wants, so every component written this way ports mechanically when the migration issue is picked up. Every new .css file is one more thing to unpick.

rules.title: Write components element-shaped
rules.rule: Props in, markup out. No module-scope side effects, no globals, and setup returns its own cleanup function.
rules.why: The stack decision is native custom elements, light DOM only (DECISIONS.md ADR-023). This shape IS the connectedCallback/disconnectedCallback lifecycle contract; components written this way need no rework, components written as IIFEs that reach into document are a rewrite.

rules.title: The three.js universe is shared primitives, not new scenes
rules.rule: A new planet, star layer, satellite, or other space-backdrop visual is built by composing the existing primitives through their props. Never hand-roll a new WebGLRenderer/Scene, or a second planet- or star-drawing function, to get a different look.
rules.why: CardPlanetRenderer (issue #61) reuses the same PlanetBody class as the <st-planet-field> backdrop instead of writing a second drawPlanet() -- the thing the pre-#61 code did three times (script.js, arcade/arcade.js, arcade/shared/starfield.js) before rule-of-three would have caught it. The prop surface already covers most requests a new visual wants; adding a class to get a look the existing one can already produce with different props recreates that cluster.

one planet: position (s0, px), parallax (pf), depth, spin, ring/earth/bands flags, per-planet colours
primitives.PlanetFieldElement / <st-planet-field> -: a full backdrop: planets[], starLayers[], drift, focusY, driven/interactive/satellites attributes
primitives.CardPlanetRenderer -- card-planet-render: many small planet icons sharing one WebGL context, same PlanetBody
primitives.planet-textures.ts: surfaceTexture/cloudTexture/ringTexture/streakTexture/glowTexture generate every planet or star texture in the repo; rand() is the seeded PRNG that keeps every sky deterministic -- never Math.random() here

rules.$primitives: Play with position, parallax and depth, and star-layer density/alpha, before reaching for a new file -- that space is large and mostly unexplored. A visual the existing props genuinely cannot produce is a rule-of-three conversation, not a silent new class.
rules.knownResolved: drawPlanet was a x3 cluster (script.js, arcade/arcade.js, arcade/shared/starfield.js) before #61; the backdrop copies are gone. One remains -- nebula-trail.js still imports the 2D drawPlanet() from arcade/shared/starfield.js for its in-game visual -- which is a single isolated usage, not a cluster, and out of scope for this rule since it's Canvas 2D, not three.js.

gates.$comment: Which gates run at which rung. Mirrors envs.json. The asymmetry IS the prototyping balance: sloppy code reaches a preview URL in ninety seconds, and gets cleaned on the way to stage.
